And now they want us to pay $199/year??. I’ve been a loyal [APP] customer for several years. This app has been a good budget tool with reliable account connections.   However, [APP] has always sorely missed planning features like goal planning and retirement planning.  As of an email this evening, they finally released these features, only now I’d have to pay an extra $100/year to access them ($199 total).  That is a crazy ask for a feature that should be standard with a standard $99 annual plan.  

Sure the new “[APP] Plus” gives a free Will creation and a few business-specific features, but no one asked for that.

Budget forecasting and planning are standard features that no one should have to pay extra for.  It looks like new [APP] subscribers can look forward to future upcharges for any forthcoming new features.  Just wait for the new “[APP] Plus with AI” product coming next month.

Cancel my subscription - poor customer support and disappointing business practices.. I’ve been a [APP] customer for several years, but I’ve decided to cancel my subscription. Over the past few months, I’ve noticed a decline in the service and feature improvements.

Things got worse in April when they introduced a two-tier system that wasn’t available to [MARCA] subscribers. To add insult to injury, when you switch to direct billing, you can’t access the monthly subscription for the higher package. Instead, you’re forced to go straight to the $200-per-year option (plus tax). The base package is still available as either monthly or yearly.

Overall, it feels like they’re trying to extract more money from customers while offering fewer features, and that’s disappointing. I’m not sure what’s going on inside the company, but it looks like they don’t have their business in order. It’s too bad, because they started well, but it’s time to move on to a different service.

If my data comes through, then I have a cluttered, confusing interface to fight through before anything useful can be realized. What a mess. Don’t waste your money.

2 Stars for the iPad App / 4.5 stars for the platform. I absolutely love the platform and experience very issues with syncing but I absolutely hate the iPad app’s unnecessarily reduced capabilities and minimal investment in improving it. Over a year ago I requested that the reporting feature from the web version be brought to the iPad, which at that time was the only major feature missing from the iPad, and this month got notified that it has been delivered to “mobile”. After redownloading the iPad app, which I deleted for lack of feature parity, I discovered that “mobile” appears to only mean “phones” and not tablets. Super let down, especially given that now in addition to reports there are a bunch of business features that are not available on iPad/tablets. Not trying to throw shade, but if [APP] isn’t going to maintain feature parity between devices then they shouldn’t offer apps for them.

Opening different menus, reports, changing categories, etc. happens so slowly with no feedback anything is happening. So the worst part is you tap a transaction, for instance, nothing happens, no loading symbol, no feedback of any kind. So you think your phone just didnt register your touch maybe? So you go to tap the same thing, still nothing, tap tap tap. EVENTUALLY it will load, but all those other taps you did? Those were all queued, so once the app finally decides to open the thing you wanted, it also opens up 10+ duplicates of the same thing, which you have to close manually.

The slow loading is already a massive annoyance that didnt used to be a thing for the last 3 years I've been using this app, but the experience around it with no feedback, and then flooding you with the same page repeatedly after not responding, is making me want to find a new finance app if the developers can't fix it. Like every budget app, it sucks. [APP] on it’s surface looks great but like every other money app, they focus on features for budgeting long term, but fail to get the month to month right and thus failing to budget forecast correctly. 

One example: [APP] forces your accounts to show statement amounts when sync’d. So for ex: I may have 3 credit cards, one with $1,000, one with $2,000, and one with $3,000 balances. [APP] surfaces this data as “you owe $6,000 this month” and shows the monthly recurring dollar amount as something atrociously high. 

The statement amount and payment amount are not the same thing - the fact that you cant extrapolate that data automatically is one thing. But the fact that I cant MANUALLY set it either makes this app a complete waste of money. $100 a year for an app that can’t get the month to month numbers right is wild.
